content.content:
One row per physical Proxmox host: `apiUrl`/`tokenId`/`tokenSecret` (a scoped Proxmox API token — every
VM-level operation goes through this, via `pveFor(conn)`/`pveForNode(node)` in `lib/proxmox.ts`, never
raw SSH), `publicIp`, `natChain`/`bridge`/`subnetPrefix` (this node's own NAT island — see below),
`provider`/`region`/`providerServerId`, `isPrimary`/`enabled`/`status`. Contrast with `HostingNode` (the
separate shared-hosting product), which has real SSH fields (`sshHost`/`sshPort`/`rootPasswordEnc`) —
a deliberate difference in trust model between the two products, not an inconsistency to "fix" by
converging them.

### The NAT-island principle

Each node NATs its **own** private `/24` (`10.20.N.0/24`) behind its **own** public IP. This makes each
node fully self-sufficient for provisioning, IP allocation, and SSH DNAT — but it does **not** give VMs
on different physical hosts a shared LAN. A VM on node-1 cannot reach a VM on node-2 over the private
network; they are separate NAT islands unless a future WireGuard/VXLAN overlay is built (not needed for
independent single-node-per-customer VPS/game hosting, which is the common case today).

### Standing rules for any new per-server code

1. **Any new Proxmox API call for a specific server must go through `pveFor`/`pveForNode`**, never the
   bare singleton functions in `lib/proxmox.ts` — those exist only as a same-behavior fallback for the
   (rare, and shrinking) case where a `Server` row genuinely has no `node` relation.
2. **Any new SSH/SFTP/RCON call site must select both `dedicatedIp` and `node`** on its `Server` query
   and pass both through to `connectionTarget()` (`lib/sftp.ts`) — this is the one choke point that
   decides where a guest connection actually goes. Do not add a new direct-dial pattern (a past mistake,
   made three separate times, that all had to be found and unwound in the 2026-09-05 audit) — always go
   through `withServerSsh`/`exec` (`lib/ssh-exec.ts`).
3. **Any new host-level operation** (iptables, a file that must land on the node's own local disk, a
   local shell command like `zfs`/`pvesm`/`qm` run outside the Proxmox REST API) **cannot be done from
   the worker directly for a non-primary node** — the worker process runs only on the primary. It must
   go through the per-node agent (see below, live since Phase 3) — extend the agent with a new endpoint
   rather than reaching for SSH, which this codebase deliberately does not use to reach a `Node`.
4. **Run a real `tsc --noEmit` before trusting any change that touches `worker/*.ts`.** The deploy
   pipeline's own build (`next build`) only compiles the Next.js app's module graph — it does not
   type-check the worker, which runs under `tsx` with no separate compile step. A type error
   introduced in worker code would pass `deploy-staging.sh` cleanly and only surface at runtime,
   possibly mid-job. `npx tsc` in the repo root is safe to run directly (the project's `tsconfig.json`
   already sets `noEmit: true`, so it writes nothing) — this is a different operation from `next build`
   and does **not** fall under the "never build in the live prod tree" rule, which is specifically about
   `.next` artifacts.

### The node-agent (Class-B fixes) — live since Phase 3, 2026-09-05

A small, scoped, dependency-free HTTPS service (`node-agent/index.js`, plain JS — not TypeScript —
so a freshly onboarded node with no copy of this repo and no npm packages can still run it),
installed on every non-primary node by `scripts/onboard-node.sh`, authenticated with its own bearer
token. **Encrypted, not hashed**, on `Node.agentTokenEnc` (`lib/crypto-box.ts`, AES-256-GCM) — unlike
`lib/telemetry-token.ts`'s hash-at-rest pattern, because the trust direction is reversed: a telemetry
token flows server-calls-primary (primary is the verifier, so a hash suffices), while the node-agent
token flows primary-calls-node (the primary is the one who must PRESENT the token on every request,
so it has to be decryptable — the same requirement `Node.tokenSecret`, the Proxmox token, already
has). The primary itself never runs this agent. Endpoints: `GET /v1/health`; the four
`lib/nat-rules.ts` `NatHost` primitives (`ensure-chain`, `chain/:chain` GET, `nat/rule` POST/DELETE,
reusing `NatRule` verbatim) so `worker/network.ts`'s already-tested NAT reconciliation logic gets a
remote transport with zero changes to the tested logic itself; `POST/DELETE /v1/snippet` for the
cloud-init vendor-snippet write (filename allowlisted to exactly `nxeon-<vmid>.yaml`); `GET
/v1/iptables/dnat-check` for the dedicated-IP double-allocation guard. HTTPS with a self-signed cert
(the primary connects with certificate verification disabled — the same trust model already used for
this node's own Proxmox API). Bound to the node's own public IP, restricted by that node's own
firewall to accept connections only from the primary's public IP — see the incident note inside
`scripts/firewall-node.nft` for a real lockout-class bug this rule went through before it shipped,
and why the fix put the agent-port rule in the SAME chain as the admin-port rules rather than a
second base chain. Covered by `test/node-agent.test.ts` (spawns the real file, drives it with real
HTTPS requests, real throwaway `iptables`/Proxmox-snippet mutations).

### Multi-node disaster-recovery backups (2026-09-12)

**Starting point, discovered while building this**: `scripts/backup-offsite.sh` had never actually
replicated anything anywhere, since the day it was written — it failed every single run
(`nxeon-backup-offsite.service`, 04:20 daily) because no target was ever configured in
`/etc/nxeon/backup-offsite.env`, and it correctly hard-fails rather than silently "succeeding" (see
that script's own header for the 2026-07-24..26 incident this behavior was built to prevent). So the
platform had zero off-site backup coverage of anything, ever, until this date. Separately, node-2 and
node-3 had zero **local** backup coverage either — `scripts/backup-vms.sh`/`backup-pve-config.sh` only
ever ran on the primary, so a node-2 or node-3 chassis loss would have lost every VM on it with no
recovery path at all, local or remote.

**What closed both gaps, in order:**

1. **An actual off-site target.** Dropbox (Plus plan, 1-month trial), via `rclone` — chosen by the
   owner over Backblaze B2/Wasabi/Hetzner Storage Box/Mega after a cost comparison (B2 ≈ $6/TB/mo is
   cheaper and better-suited to unattended automation, but Dropbox was already available with a free
   trial). Configured via `rclone authorize "dropbox"` (OAuth, with a refresh token — NOT the Dropbox
   App Console's one-off "Generate access token" button, which typically has no refresh token and would
   silently stop working after ~4h). `backup-offsite.sh` applies gentler `--transfers`/`--tpslimit`
   flags specifically for a `dropbox:` remote — its API rate-limits automated bulk syncs more
   aggressively than B2/S3-compatible backends, especially on personal-tier accounts.
2. **Local backups on every node, not just the primary.** `backup-vms.sh`/`backup-pve-config.sh`
   needed zero code changes to run on node-2/node-3 — they were already fully parameterized (pure
   Proxmox-CLI bash, no app/DB dependency) and already default to the exact directory
   (`/tank/backup`) every node's own HDD storage already uses. `scripts/onboard-node.sh` gained a new
   step 9 ("Local disaster-recovery backups") installing them + `nxeon-backup-vms.timer` on any future
   node automatically; node-2 and node-3 were retrofitted by hand the same way. The `OnFailure=nxeon-alert@%n.service`
   hook on this unit is a harmless no-op on a non-primary node (that unit only exists on the primary,
   which runs the app/DB `alert-admins.sh` needs) — systemd logs "ignoring: Unit ... not found" and
   moves on; it does not fail the backup job itself.
3. **A real, pre-existing bug this surfaced**: node-2's and node-3's cloud-init OS templates
   (VMID 9000-9004ish) carry `cicustom: vendor=backup:snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` — copied verbatim from
   the primary's convention, where a Proxmox storage literally named `backup` exists. Neither node-2 nor
   node-3 had ever had a storage by that name (their `/tank/backup` directory is registered as
   `vmdata-hdd` instead), so `vzdump`'s own config-validation pass failed every template backup with
   `storage 'backup' does not exist`. Fixed by adding a second, `snippets`-only `dir` storage named
   `backup` on both nodes, pointing at the same `/tank/backup` path their real `vmdata-hdd` storage
   already uses (scoping its content to `snippets` only avoids double-indexing the same vzdump archives
   under two storage IDs). This was blocking template backups specifically — it does not appear to have
   broken cloud-init on real customer VMs cloned from these templates (they were provisioning and
   booting correctly beforehand), but a dangling storage reference in a template's own config is worth
   knowing about regardless if cloud-init is ever re-triggered against it.
4. **The node-agent (`node-agent/index.js`) gained two new read-only endpoints**: `GET
   /v1/backup/manifest` (lists this node's own local backup files — host-config archives + vzdump
   archives — under an allowlist regex matching exactly what `backup-pve-config.sh`/`backup-vms.sh`
   produce) and `GET /v1/backup/file?path=...` (streams one file's raw bytes, with the same
   resolve-and-confirm-it's-really-under-the-backup-root defense `resolveSnippetPath()` already used for
   snippets). Unlike every other agent endpoint, these are pull-only — the primary never writes anything
   through them.
5. **`scripts/collect-node-backups.ts`** (new, runs on the primary) — for every enabled non-primary
   `Node`, calls its agent's manifest endpoint, downloads anything new/changed into
   `/tank/backup/nodes/<node-name>/<platform|status>/...`, and deletes local copies of anything the
   node's own manifest no longer lists (mirrors that node's own `KEEP_LAST` retention onto the collected
   copy, so this tree's size tracks the source rather than growing forever). Runs as "step 0" of
   `backup-offsite.sh`, before the Dropbox sync, so a fresh node backup reaches Dropbox the same night
   it was made. A single unreachable node is recorded in
   `/tank/backup/status/node-collect.json` and does NOT fail the primary's own db/host-config/vms sync —
   same per-node honesty-banner instinct `lib/monitoring.ts`'s `nodeStorageUsage()` already uses
   elsewhere, rather than one merged pass/fail that could hide a silently-broken single node forever.
6. **Dropbox is organized one numbered, dated folder per RUN, and one subfolder per node inside it**
   (owner's explicit design, 2026-09-12 afternoon, superseding the first same-day cut which used one
   persistent folder per node with no date grouping): `<remote>/00001-2026-09-12/primary/{db,host-config,vms}/`,
   `<remote>/00001-2026-09-12/<node-name>/{platform,status}/` for every other node. The counter
   (`/tank/backup/status/offsite-run-number`) is monotonic and survives failed runs (a failed run still
   consumes a number rather than risking two runs racing for the same folder name). Critically, each
   run only uploads files that are **new since the last fully successful run** (tracked by
   `/tank/backup/status/offsite-last-run-marker`, a timestamp file touched only once every label has
   succeeded) — duplicating a full local mirror (which itself holds 3 retained generations) into a
   fresh dated folder every single day would have multiplied the daily VM-archive upload 3x for zero
   benefit, since those bytes already exist under a previous run's folder. A run with nothing new for
   a label (e.g. a manual re-run the same day) simply omits that label rather than failing or uploading
   duplicate data; a run that fails partway does NOT advance the marker, so a retry re-attempts exactly
   what was missed. Old run-folders beyond `OFFSITE_KEEP_RUNS` (owner's choice: 7 — deliberately more
   than each local script's own keep-last=3, since remote history is cheap under this delta model) are
   pruned automatically after each successful run. `sync_one()`'s own file-count precheck/post-check
   had to switch from `find -maxdepth 1` to a plain recursive `find` to handle a per-node label being a
   small tree (`platform/`/`status/` subdirs) rather than a flat directory of files.
   **Migration note**: the very first cut of this (same day, run manually before the redesign) left a
   one-time legacy `db/`, `host-config/`, `vms/` flat folder set on Dropbox, from before run-numbering
   existed. It was left in place rather than auto-deleted (still real, restorable data) — the automatic
   pruning above only ever touches folders matching the `NNNNN-YYYY-MM-DD` pattern, so it will never
   touch those three by accident. The run marker was seeded to "now" at the moment of the redesign
   specifically so the first numbered run wouldn't re-upload everything already sitting in that legacy
   set.
7. **`/opt/nxeon/.env` — the app's own secrets (DB URL, AUTH_SECRET, API keys) — was captured nowhere
   until this date**, distinct from `/etc/nxeon` (the backup/firewall/mail config a systemd job reads,
   which WAS already captured). Added to `backup-pve-config.sh`'s optional-extras list (present-only,
   like the others there, since only the primary runs the app).

**What still isn't covered, honestly**: a node's OWN backup unit going red (disk full, vzdump wedged)
is not yet alerted anywhere on that node itself — `alert-admins.sh` needs the app/DB and only exists on
the primary. The intended signal path is `collect-node-backups.ts` noticing a node's manifest is stale
or empty and that showing up in `/admin/backups`, but that admin-panel-side rendering (the Phase 4 item
from the original 2026-09-05 multi-node plan — "loop all nodes, merge into a per-node view, render with
the same 'some nodes unreachable' honesty-banner pattern `app/admin/backups/page.tsx`'s customer-backup
section already uses") has not been built yet; today `node-collect.json` exists and is accurate, but
nothing in the UI reads it yet.

**Restoring from any of this** — the database, host config, a VM, or a brand-new node — is a separate,
dedicated runbook: `docs/DISASTER-RECOVERY.md`. It also documents what already runs, unattended and
proven, today: `nxeon-verify-restore.timer` restores the newest local DB dump into a real scratch
database every night and asserts real rows came back — the restore path is not theoretical.

Documentation=https://nxeon.local/docs
After=network-online.target pve-cluster.service

[Service]
Type=simple
# Root is required: this service shells out to iptables (NAT table) and
# pvesm/writes files under a Proxmox storage's snippets directory, neither of
# which a restricted service account can do on a Proxmox host. The blast
# radius of the process itself is bounded elsewhere — narrow, allowlisted
# operations (node-agent/index.js's own input validation), a single scoped
# bearer token (not the Proxmox API token), and network exposure restricted
# to the primary's public IP by this node's own firewall (see
# scripts/onboard-node.sh's agent-allow step).
User=root
Group=root
WorkingDirectory=/opt/nxeon-agent
EnvironmentFile=/etc/nxeon/node-agent.env
ExecStart=/usr/bin/node /opt/nxeon-agent/index.js
Restart=always
RestartSec=3

# --- Hardening --------------------------------------------------------------
# Root is necessary (see above), so hardening here narrows WHAT root-level
# access this specific process gets, not whether it has any.
NoNewPrivileges=true
ProtectHome=true
PrivateTmp=true
ProtectKernelTunables=true
ProtectKernelModules=true
ProtectControlGroups=true
RestrictSUIDSGID=true
LockPersonality=true
# NOT ProtectSystem=strict: this process must write into whichever directory
# pvesm resolves a storage's snippets path to, which varies per node
# (HDD_DIR from onboard-node.sh) and cannot be enumerated in advance here.

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
[Unit]
Description=Nxeon daily whole-system backup (host config + every guest, ~04:30)
# ROOT CAUSE THIS FILE FIXES — whole-system backups had NEVER run.
#
# This timer previously read `OnCalendar=Sun *-*-* 04:30:00`. It was enabled at
# 2026-07-23 11:36:20 UTC, a THURSDAY, so its first eligible fire was Sunday
# 2026-07-26 04:30 — three days later. `Persistent=true` did not back-fill,
# because Persistent= only replays an elapse that was *missed while the timer was
# inactive*, and that is computed from
# /var/lib/systemd/timers/stamp-nxeon-backup-vms.timer, which did not exist until
# the first genuine trigger wrote it. A never-triggered timer has no missed
# elapse to replay. Nothing was misconfigured; the weekly schedule itself
# guaranteed a multi-day window in which a live host with real customer VMs held
# zero whole-VM backups, and `OnFailure=nxeon-alert@` could not report it because
# a unit that never runs never fails.
#
# Daily is the owner's stated cadence ("back up the entire system once every day,
# store the latest 3") and it also bounds this failure class: the worst case for a
# freshly installed daily timer is under 24 hours instead of a week.
#
# After enabling this timer, run the unit once by hand — `systemctl start
# nxeon-backup-vms.service` — rather than waiting for the window. /admin/backups
# flags any timer whose LastTriggerUSec is empty precisely so this is visible.

[Timer]
OnCalendar=*-*-* 04:30:00
Persistent=true
RandomizedDelaySec=600

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
[Unit]
Description=Nxeon host firewall (nftables)
After=network-pre.target
Before=network.target
Wants=network-pre.target

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/usr/sbin/nft -f /opt/nxeon/scripts/firewall.nft
ExecReload=/usr/sbin/nft -f /opt/nxeon/scripts/firewall.nft
RemainAfterExit=yes
# Revert easily: systemctl stop nxeon-firewall  (then nft delete table inet nxeon_fw)
ExecStop=/usr/sbin/nft delete table inet nxeon_fw

[Install]

#!/bin/bash
# Nxeon — build additional Proxmox cloud-init templates
# Mirrors exactly how templates 9000/9001 were built:
#   scsi0 on vmdata via import-from, ide2 cloudinit, vmbr1 net, agent enabled,
#   serial0 socket + vga serial0, cicustom vendor snippet, then `qm template`.
# Downloads cloud images to /var/lib/vz/template/cloudimg/ and registers each
# template in the OsTemplate table of both the nxeon and nxeon_staging DBs.
# Idempotent: skips builds where the VMID already exists; DB upserts on slug.
set -euo pipefail

IMGDIR="/var/lib/vz/template/cloudimg"
STORAGE="vmdata"
VENDOR="backup:snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml"
DBS=(nxeon nxeon_staging)

mkdir -p "$IMGDIR"
log() { echo "[$(date +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z)] $*"; }

# template spec: VMID | slug | display name | filename | url
TEMPLATES=(
  "9002|almalinux-9|AlmaLinux 9|AlmaLinux-9-GenericCloud-latest.x86_64.qcow2|https://repo.almalinux.org/almalinux/9/cloud/x86_64/images/AlmaLinux-9-GenericCloud-latest.x86_64.qcow2"
  "9003|rocky-9|Rocky Linux 9|Rocky-9-GenericCloud-Base.latest.x86_64.qcow2|https://download.rockylinux.org/pub/rocky/9/images/x86_64/Rocky-9-GenericCloud-Base.latest.x86_64.qcow2"
  "9004|ubuntu-22-04|Ubuntu 22.04 LTS|jammy-server-cloudimg-amd64.img|https://cloud-images.ubuntu.com/jammy/current/jammy-server-cloudimg-amd64.img"
)

register_db() {
    local slug="$1" name="$2" vmid="$3"
    for db in "${DBS[@]}"; do
        sudo -u postgres psql -d "$db" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -c \
"INSERT INTO \"OsTemplate\" (id,slug,name,vmid,active)
 VALUES (md5(random()::text || clock_timestamp()::text), '${slug}', '${name}', ${vmid}, true)
 ON CONFLICT (slug) DO UPDATE SET vmid=excluded.vmid, name=excluded.name, active=true;" \
        && log "registered '${slug}' (vmid ${vmid}) in DB '${db}'"
    done
}

build_one() {
    local vmid="$1" slug="$2" name="$3" fname="$4" url="$5"
    local img="${IMGDIR}/${fname}"

    if qm status "$vmid" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        log "VMID ${vmid} (${slug}) already exists — skipping build, re-registering DB"
        register_db "$slug" "$name" "$vmid"
        return 0
    fi

    log "downloading ${name} image"
    if ! wget -q --show-progress -O "${img}.partial" "$url"; then
        log "ERROR: download failed for ${name} (${url}) — skipping"
        rm -f "${img}.partial"
        return 1
    fi
    mv "${img}.partial" "$img"

    log "creating VM ${vmid} (${name})"
    qm create "$vmid" \
        --name "tpl-${slug}" \
        --memory 1024 \
        --cores 1 \
        --cpu host \
# Nxeon multi-node synergy — full audit + hardening plan

## Context

Nxeon just grew from one Proxmox compute node (primary, OVH Singapore) to two (node-2, Hetzner Falkenstein, onboarded today). Enabling node-2 for real traffic surfaced one confirmed bug (the worker's NAT/port-forward sync only ever touches the primary's own iptables). The owner asked: "the primary node needs to be able to have complete control of all of the nodes, complete sync, am I right?" — yes, and a full platform-wide audit (3 parallel deep-research passes + 1 design pass, all cross-verified against live code) found this is bigger than one bug: **one shared root-cause function** (`lib/sftp.ts`'s `connectionTarget()`) silently breaks nearly the entire SSH-based customer control panel for any server not on the primary node, plus several independent gaps (a live firewall-hardening exposure on node-2 right now, zero disaster-recovery backup coverage for node-2, a backup-download 404-class bug, a stale vmid-collision risk). Zero real customers have ever been provisioned onto node-2 (confirmed via DB), so every fix below can be built and proven safely before it matters to anyone. node-2 is currently `enabled: false` in the DB (disabled earlier today as an immediate protective measure) and should stay that way until Phase 0 + Phase 1 land.

## Ground truth (verified against live code and the live host, not assumed)

- **Architecture**: `Node` model (schema.prisma:1151) — one row per physical Proxmox host (`apiUrl`/`tokenId`/`tokenSecret`/`publicIp`/`natChain`/`bridge`/`subnetPrefix`/`provider`/`region`). VM-level operations are ALREADY correctly multi-node via `pveFor`/`pveForNode` (lib/proxmox.ts) — that part of today's earlier rollout is solid. There is exactly ONE worker process for the whole platform (`worker/index.ts`, systemd unit `nxeon-worker`), running only on the primary — confirmed via package.json, CLAUDE.md, and `onboard-node.sh`'s own header, which already documents each node as a separate NAT island with no cross-node private networking.
- **Bug Class A (pure code fix, no new infra)**: `lib/sftp.ts:35-41` (`SftpServer` type) has no `node` field; `connectionTarget()` (~line 137) resolves a non-dedicated-IP server's SSH host as `process.env.PUBLIC_IP` (the primary's IP), never `server.node.publicIp`. Verified live — the type and doc comment match exactly. This one function underpins `lib/ssh-exec.ts`'s `withServerSsh()`/`exec()` and `lib/sftp.ts`'s `withSftp()`, which are the shared SSH plumbing for: the web terminal, file manager, game console/RCON/kick/ban, game power/backup/scheduled-restart/player-tracking (worker sweeps firing every ~60s), the cPanel-lite control panel (websites/DBs/services/one-click apps/static-site publish), SSL issuance, game mods/config, the guest-side half of disk-expand/volume-attach, migration data-copy, the fleet SSH-health sweep (fires every ~15min), and the free-Minecraft shared host. Two call sites already do this correctly and prove the fix pattern: `worker/index.ts:712,814` and `worker/game-subdomain-sync.ts`'s `resolveGameServerDnsTarget()`. `worker/volumes.ts` and `worker/disk-expand.ts` **already select `node`** for their Proxmox calls — they self-heal for free the moment the root fix lands. Three files (`worker/claude.ts`, `worker/game-update.ts`, `worker/firewall.ts`) bypass `connectionTarget` entirely with an even more broken pattern (direct dial to the guest's *private* `10.20.x.x` IP, which the primary has no route to for node-2) — these fold into the same fix once rewritten onto `withServerSsh`.
- **Bug Class B (needs new infrastructure — the worker has no OS-level access to a second physical machine)**: (1) `worker/network.ts`'s `syncPortForwards()`/`reconcileNatChain()` rebuilds NAT/DNAT iptables rules via local `execFile("iptables",...)` — only ever the primary's kernel. (2) `worker/index.ts`'s `provision()` writes the per-VM cloud-init vendor snippet via local `fs.writeFile()` — a VM provisioned on node-2 is told to read a snippet that only ever landed on the primary's disk, so it boots and reports "ready" while its setup script silently never ran. (3) `lib/dedicated-ip.ts`'s `hasLiveDnatRule()` checks the primary's local iptables before allocating a dedicated IP — for a node-2 IP this checks the wrong host, risking a double-allocation.
- **Separate, independent bugs**: `lib/monitoring.ts`'s `backupSummary()` merges every node's backup listing into one scalar, so a healthy primary backup masks a silently-broken node-2 backup schedule forever (sibling function `nodeStorageUsage()` in the same file already does this correctly, per-node, unmerged — copy that shape). `lib/platform-backups.ts` (admin disaster-recovery panel) reads only local files on whichever box the web app runs on — zero node-2 awareness, and the *customer*-backup half of that same admin page already has the correct per-node loop + "some nodes unreachable" honesty banner to copy. `app/api/servers/[id]/backups/download/route.ts` checks tenancy correctly per-node but then reads the archive bytes from a hardcoded local path — 502s for every node-2 server's backup download. At least one `Server` row (`minecraft-mm8w85`, confirmed in docs/QA-PRELAUNCH.md) has `nodeId: null`, which is a live vmid-collision risk now that a second node genuinely exists.
- **Firewall — corrected finding, better news than first suspected**: the primary already runs a mature, incident-hardened system, confirmed live and running right now: `nxeon-firewall.service` (active), `fail2ban.service` (active), `scripts/firewall.nft`, `scripts/admin-ip.sh`, `scripts/firewall-safe-apply.sh`, `scripts/firewall-reachability.sh`. None of it was ever packaged into `scripts/onboard-node.sh` or checked into `deploy/` as an installable unit template — so node-2 almost certainly has none of it. This is "port a proven system," not "build one from scratch."
- **Security-posture precedent already in this codebase**: `Node` deliberately has no SSH fields (only a scoped API token), unlike the separate `HostingNode` model which does have SSH fields for a different product with a different trust model. `lib/telemetry-token.ts`'s `mintTelemetryToken()`/hash-stored-not-plaintext pattern is the existing precedent for minting a new per-entity bearer credential.

## Decisions

- **Class B gets a lightweight per-node HTTP agent with its own bearer token — not SSH.** This preserves the existing "every physical host is reached via a narrow, token-authenticated API" invariant (matching `Node`'s existing Proxmox-token design, not `HostingNode`'s SSH design), keeps the blast radius of a leaked credential to ~6 named operations instead of an arbitrary root shell, and slots directly into `lib/nat-rules.ts`'s already-built-and-tested `NatHost` interface (`ensureChain`/`listChain`/`addRule`/`deleteRule`) with zero changes to the tested reconciliation logic in `reconcileNatChain()` — only a new transport implementation.
- **Firewall remediation ships first, out-of-band from the staged rollout** — it's a live exposure, not an architecture gap, and the fix is "copy 4 scripts + 1 systemd unit," not new engineering.
- **`nodeId: null` backfill ships first too** — one-time, low-risk, fully decoupled from everything else.
- **Both documentation deliverables are written incrementally as each phase lands**, not once at the end — matching this repo's own stated convention that docs update in the same commit as the change.
- **node-2 stays `enabled: false`** until Phase 0 and Phase 1 are live and verified against a real throwaway test server.

## Phase 0 — Immediate, today, out-of-band from everything else

1. **Firewall port to node-2**: copy `firewall.nft`, `admin-ip.sh`, `firewall-safe-apply.sh`, `firewall-reachability.sh` + install `fail2ban` + `/etc/fail2ban/jail.d/nxeon.conf` onto node-2. Seed `/etc/nxeon/admin-ips.nft` from the primary's populated list. **Deliberate posture difference from the primary**: the primary intentionally leaves SSH (22) public (fail2ban-protected only) as a recovery channel of last resort for its public web app; node-2 is a pure compute node with no such need, so set its admin-allowlist to cover **both** 22 and 8006. Document this reasoning inline in the ported script so it reads as a decision. Apply via `firewall-safe-apply.sh`'s full `--check`/`--apply`/verify-from-fresh-connection/`--confirm` flow — never a raw `nft -f`.
2. **`nodeId: null` backfill**: find every `Server` with `nodeId: null`, confirm each vmid is genuinely live on the primary's `pveNode` via the Proxmox API, set `nodeId` to the primary's id. Model the script on `scripts/backfill-claude.ts`'s shape.
3. **Write both documentation deliverables' initial version now** (see Documentation section below) — the retrospective can be written in full immediately (it's describing completed work); the permanent reference doc gets its skeleton + sections 1-2 now, filled in further as each later phase lands.

## Phase 1 — Class A root fix + highest-value call sites

1. Fix `lib/sftp.ts`: add `node?: { publicIp: string } | null` to `SftpServer`; change `connectionTarget()`'s non-dedicated branch to `server.node?.publicIp ?? process.env.PUBLIC_IP ?? ""`. Keep `node` optional (preserves today's exact fallback behavior for any row that's genuinely primary-only).
2. Verify `worker/volumes.ts`/`worker/disk-expand.ts` self-heal (no code change — they already select `node`).
3. Thread `node: { select: { publicIp: true } }` into the query for, in order: `worker/ssh-health.ts` (stops false fleet-wide alerts first), `lib/actions-game-control.ts` + `worker/game-control.ts` (highest-frequency customer surface), `terminal-server/index.ts` + `lib/actions-files.ts` + `app/api/files/[serverId]/route.ts` (web terminal + file manager).
4. Prove the pattern end-to-end against a real throwaway test server provisioned on node-2 before moving to Phase 2.

## Phase 2 — Remaining Class A sites + the 3 rewrites + backupSummary (parallelizable)

1. `worker/websites.ts`'s shared `sshServer()` (fixes it + `site-publish.ts` + `apps.ts` for free), `worker/databases.ts`, `worker/services.ts`, `worker/ssl.ts`.
2. `worker/game-mods.ts` (currently inert, behind `ENABLE_REAL_GAMEMODS`) + `worker/game-config.ts` (type + trace to the underlying query).
3. `lib/claude-backfill.ts` / `scripts/backfill-claude.ts`, `lib/actions-free-minecraft.ts`'s `freemcHost()` (1-line, removes a landmine even though not exercised until that host moves).
4. Rewrite `worker/claude.ts`, `worker/game-update.ts`, `worker/firewall.ts` onto `withServerSsh`/`exec` (do this after at least one Tier-3 file from Phase 1 is proven against real node-2 traffic). Note `lib/ssh-exec.ts`'s `exec()` returns `{code,stdout,stderr}` rather than throwing — adjust each file's error handling accordingly; preserve each file's existing secret-redaction logic.
5. `lib/monitoring.ts`'s `backupSummary()`: change to return per-node results (copy `nodeStorageUsage()`'s shape in the same file, don't merge). Update its two callers (`app/admin/monitoring/page.tsx`, `worker/monitor.ts`'s staleness check) to alert per-node — add a `BACKUP` dimension to `lib/node-capacity.ts`'s existing `CapDimension` enum and route through the existing `NodeAlert` debounce/resolve machinery rather than inventing a second alerting path. This item has no dependency on the node-agent and can land any time in this window.
6. Save `worker/migrate.ts`/`migrate-real.ts`'s `connectTarget()` fix for last in this phase given the file's size and that migrations touch live customer data mid-flight — test via `scripts/migration-rehearsal.ts` before trusting it against a real customer migration onto a node-2 destination.

## Phase 3 — Node-agent build (Class B), can start day 1 in parallel with Phase 1/2 (zero file overlap)

1. New `node-agent/` service (parallel to `terminal-server/`), small HTTP(S) server. New `deploy/nxeon-node-agent.service` template.
2. Schema: `Node.agentTokenHash String?` (mint/hash pattern copied from `lib/telemetry-token.ts`, raw token shown once, stored as SHA-256 hash).
3. Endpoints (bearer auth, one primitive per `NatHost` method — keeps the tested reconciliation logic on the primary): `GET /v1/health`; `POST /v1/nat/ensure-chain`; `GET /v1/nat/chain/:chain`; `POST /v1/nat/rule` / `DELETE /v1/nat/rule` (reuse `NatRule` from `lib/nat-rules.ts` verbatim); `POST /v1/snippet` + `DELETE /v1/snippet/:filename` (filename allowlisted); `GET /v1/iptables/dnat-check?address=X`.
4. Dispatch helper (e.g. `natHostFor(node)` in `worker/network.ts`): local `iptablesHost()` when `node.isPrimary`, else an HTTP-backed `agentNatHost(node)` adapter implementing the same `NatHost` interface. The primary itself never runs the agent.
5. Network exposure: agent bound to the node's public IP, gated by that node's own nftables to accept connections only from the primary's public IP (same single-source-allow mechanism `admin-ip.sh` already implements for 8006 — a new set, not the human admin allowlist).
6. Admin UI: extend `/admin/nodes/new`, `addNode()`/`updateNode()` (lib/actions-nodes.ts) with an agent-token field (hashed immediately, never redisplayed); extend `testNode()` to also probe `GET /v1/health`.
7. Extend `scripts/onboard-node.sh` with a new step: ship the bundled agent, generate+write the token (0600), install+enable the systemd unit, add the primary's IP to the node's agent-port allowlist, print the token in the same "Add node" form block the script already prints.
8. Wire real callers: `worker/network.ts` (NAT sync), `worker/index.ts`'s `provision()` (snippet write), `lib/dedicated-ip.ts`'s `hasLiveDnatRule()` (dnat-check) — each dispatches to the agent only for non-primary nodes.
9. Real end-to-end test: provision a throwaway NAT-based game server on node-2, confirm `iptables -t nat -S NXEON_FWD` on node-2 itself shows the rule, then prove it externally (connect from a third machine to node-2's public IP). Confirm a fresh node-2 provision actually ran its setup script (MOTD/guest-agent/telemetry shipper present).

## Phase 4 — Agent-dependent bugs

1. Extend the agent with `GET /v1/backup/:filename` (stream bytes, reuse the download route's existing `ARCHIVE_RE`/basename-confinement checks) and `GET /v1/backup-status`.

import type { NodeProvider } from "@prisma/client";

/**
 * Valid datacenter-code per provider, plus a human-readable label for each.
 * `Node.region` is a plain string (not an enum) because datacenter codes
 * grow far more often than providers do — same "fast-changing categorical
 * value, validated in code not the DB" convention this schema already uses
 * for StaffGrant.area (see lib/staff-grants.ts). Validate any new/edited
 * Node's region against `NODE_REGIONS[provider]` rather than trusting a
 * free-typed string from the admin form.
 *
 * Codes are each provider's OWN real datacenter code (OVH's/Hetzner's own
 * naming), not a platform-invented scheme — "sgp1" (OVH Singapore, where the
 * primary node actually is — confirmed via geoip-lite against its live
 * public IP, not guessed) and "fsn1" (Hetzner Falkenstein, Germany, the new
 * node) are both real. The other codes below are real provider datacenter
 * codes too, listed so the region field has somewhere to grow without a
 * schema change — add more here as real nodes are added, not speculatively.
 */
export const NODE_REGIONS = {
  OVH: ["sgp1", "bhs1", "gra1", "rbx1", "waw1"],
  HETZNER: ["fsn1", "nbg1", "hel1", "ash1", "hil1"],
} as const satisfies Record<NodeProvider, readonly string[]>;

/** Every valid region code, derived from `NODE_REGIONS`. */
export type RegionCode = (typeof NODE_REGIONS)[keyof typeof NODE_REGIONS][number];

/**
 * `REGION_LABELS` / `CUSTOMER_REGION_LABELS` / `REGION_COUNTRY` /
 * `REGION_COORDS` below are each built as a `_STRICT` const first, checked
 * with `satisfies Record<RegionCode, ...>` so `npx tsc --noEmit` fails if a
 * future region is added to `NODE_REGIONS` without a matching entry in every
 * one of these tables (a missing OR a stray/misspelled key both fail the
 * check) — then exported at the wider `Record<string, ...>` type every
 * existing call site already expects (`REGION_COUNTRY[region] ?? fallback`
 * with `region: string` straight off a DB row), so this hardening needed no
 * changes anywhere else in the codebase.
 *
 * Added 2026-09-29 during the Canada/bhs1 rollout audit. Nothing here was
 * actually found missing an entry for bhs1 — `REGION_COUNTRY` has had
 * `bhs1: "ca"` since this file was first created, well before the Canada
 * node existed — but the audit did find a SECOND, hand-copied region table
 * in components/admin/NodeForms.tsx (a client component that didn't need to
 * duplicate this at all — this file has no `server-only` import, so it can
 * be imported directly into a client component) that had nothing keeping it
 * in sync with this one. A duplicated, hand-maintained table is exactly the

Checking a few more things: node-3/5 hostnames resolve fine via hostname -f, swappiness looks consistent across nodes, and zpool scrub cron jobs should exist via the standard zfsutils-linux package — I'll confirm that's actually scheduled on primary and nodes 3-5. Looking at node-5, I'm checking why /tank/backup shows 14G on the root filesystem, tracing through the vzdump backups and the nightly onboard backup job that keeps the last 3 backups for VMs.

The real issue surfaces here: node-5's backup volume lives on the 20GB root filesystem and is 96% full, which is a critical risk for an imminent root-full outage even though today's backup succeeded. The fix should involve carving out a dedicated ZFS dataset for backups like node-3 has, and moving the existing contents over. Separately, node-2's backup timer is enabled but was apparently never started (likely enabled without --now), leaving backups stale for 19 days—another critical finding that needs a simple start command. I also want to check how the scheduler handles missing OS templates per node, looking at the baseVmid and template availability logic.

#!/bin/bash
# ============================================================================
# firewall-safe-apply.sh — apply the Nxeon nftables ruleset without stranding
#                          the person applying it
# ============================================================================
# WHY THIS EXISTS
#   /opt/nxeon/scripts/firewall.nft restricts host SSH (tcp/22) and the Proxmox
#   web UI (tcp/8006) to an allowlist of admin source addresses. This box is
#   administered exclusively over the network, from consumer ISP addresses that
#   rotate. A wrong allowlist therefore does not "cause an alert" — it locks
#   every human out of a production hypervisor carrying paying customers.
#
#   So applying is not `nft -f`. It is:
#       1. parse-check the ruleset            (changes nothing)
#       2. check that EVERY currently-connected admin SSH peer is allowlisted
#       3. arm an automatic revert on a timer, held by systemd (survives your
#          shell dying, your link dropping, and you being locked out)
#       4. apply
#       5. you prove a BRAND NEW connection works, then --confirm to disarm
#   Do nothing after step 4 and the box heals itself. That is the whole point.
#
# USAGE
#   firewall-safe-apply.sh                 same as --check (safe, the default)
#   firewall-safe-apply.sh --check         validate + preflight, apply nothing
#   firewall-safe-apply.sh --apply         preflight, arm auto-revert, apply
#   firewall-safe-apply.sh --confirm       disarm the auto-revert (keep rules)
#   firewall-safe-apply.sh --rollback      revert to the pre-allowlist ruleset
#   firewall-safe-apply.sh --status        show what is loaded / armed
#
#   Options:
#     --force        apply even if the preflight fails (you had better be on
#                    the out-of-band console when you use this)
#     --grace=SECS   auto-revert delay, default 300. Env: NXEON_FW_GRACE
#
# ORDER OF OPERATIONS FOR A REMOTE APPLY — do not improvise this
#   Terminal A (your current session):
#       /opt/nxeon/scripts/firewall-safe-apply.sh --check     # expect PASS
#       /opt/nxeon/scripts/firewall-safe-apply.sh --apply
#   >>> LEAVE TERMINAL A OPEN. Do not log out. It survives a bad ruleset
#   >>> because of the `ct state established,related accept` rule.
#   Terminal B (new connection, from the machine you administer from):
#       ssh root@51.79.162.96                                 # must succeed
#       (and load https://51.79.162.96:8006 in a browser)
#   Terminal A, only once Terminal B worked:
#       /opt/nxeon/scripts/firewall-safe-apply.sh --confirm
#
# IF YOU ARE LOCKED OUT AND THE TIMER DID NOT SAVE YOU
#   Provider out-of-band console (OVH manager -> this server -> Console/KVM
#   noVNC), which is not affected by this ruleset, then:
#       nft delete table inet nxeon_fw
# ============================================================================
set -euo pipefail

FW_FILE="/opt/nxeon/scripts/firewall.nft"
ALLOW_FILE="/etc/nxeon/admin-ips.nft"
ROLLBACK_FILE="/etc/nxeon/firewall.nft.rollback"
TABLE="inet nxeon_fw"
REVERT_UNIT="nxeon-fw-autorevert"
GRACE="${NXEON_FW_GRACE:-300}"
# This host's own public IPv4, for the "verify a new connection works" prompt
# below — auto-detected the same way onboard-node.sh detects PUBLIC_IP, so
# this script prints the RIGHT address on every node, not just the primary.
HOST_IP="${NXEON_FW_HOST_IP:-$(hostname -I 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}')}"
REACH_SCRIPT="/opt/nxeon/scripts/firewall-reachability.sh"
# Ports that must have an accept path or the apply is refused. 22 is here because
# it is the one always-reachable recovery channel on a box administered from
# rotating consumer-ISP addresses; 80/443 because losing them is an outage for
# every tenant. 8006 is deliberately NOT required — it is allowlisted by design.
REQUIRED_PORTS="${NXEON_FW_REQUIRED_PORTS:-22 80 443}"

MODE="check"
FORCE=0
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --check)    MODE="check" ;;
    --apply)    MODE="apply" ;;
    --confirm)  MODE="confirm" ;;
    --rollback) MODE="rollback" ;;
    --status)   MODE="status" ;;
    --force)    FORCE=1 ;;
    --grace=*)  GRACE="${arg#--grace=}" ;;
    -h|--help)  sed -n '2,50p' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
    *) echo "Unknown argument: $arg (try --help)" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done

say()  { printf '%s\n' "$*"; }
ok()   { printf '  [ OK ]   %s\n' "$*"; }
bad()  { printf '  [FAIL]   %s\n' "$*"; }
warn() { printf '  [WARN]   %s\n' "$*"; }

need_root() {
  [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ] || { echo "Must run as root." >&2; exit 1; }
}

# --- who is currently administering this box over SSH? ----------------------
# AUTHENTICATED sessions, from utmp (`who`) plus this shell's own SSH_* env.
# utmp is the right source: it only contains sessions that actually completed
# authentication. Deriving the list from `ss` instead would sweep in every
# brute-force attempt that happens to have a socket open at that moment —
# port 22 on this host has taken 6266 failed logins and 627 fail2ban bans, so
# that is not a hypothetical.
#
# Reading utmp rather than only $SSH_CONNECTION means (a) it survives `sudo`
# stripping the environment, and (b) it catches the OTHER administrator's
# session too, not just yours. Locking out your colleague is the same outage as
# locking out yourself.
#
# Note this deliberately does not consider customer VM SSH: that is DNAT'd from
# host tcp/20000+ straight into the guest and never touches the host's input
# chain, so nothing here can affect it.
authenticated_admin_peers() {
  { who 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/.*(\([^)]*\))[[:space:]]*$/\1/p'
    [ -n "${SSH_CONNECTION:-}" ] && awk '{print $1}' <<<"$SSH_CONNECTION"

}

# Sockets on host tcp/22 that are NOT an authenticated session. Reported for
# information only — these are overwhelmingly scanners, and they must never be
# allowed to block a legitimate apply.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# Nxeon — canonical compute-node definition (SOURCED, never executed)
# =============================================================================
# The single source of truth for "what a correct Nxeon compute node looks like".
# Both scripts/onboard-node.sh (which APPLIES it) and scripts/verify-node.sh
# (which CHECKS it) source this file, so the two can never drift apart again —
# that drift is exactly how nodes 2..5 each shipped with something different
# (role missing VM.GuestAgent.FileRead, templates 9005-9009 absent, a backup
# volume living on the 20 GB root partition, a backup timer that was enabled
# but never started, ...). Change a value HERE and both scripts follow.
#
# Pure functions + constants only: no side effects at source time, so it is safe
# to `source` from a unit test (see scripts/test-node-scripts.sh).
# =============================================================================

# ---------- Proxmox API identity ---------------------------------------------
NXEON_CANON_TOKEN_USER="nxeon@pve"
NXEON_CANON_TOKEN_NAME="platform"
NXEON_CANON_ROLE="NxeonProvision"

# The COMPLETE privilege list the platform needs (27). Derived from the live
# role on node-2..5 on 2026-10-01 after VM.GuestAgent.FileRead was added fleet
# wide. Why each one is here:
#   VM.Allocate / VM.Clone / VM.Config.*        clone a template, resize, set cloud-init, NIC, options
#   VM.Config.Options                           `qm set --agent/--onboot/--cicustom/--balloon` — the primary's own role
#                                               was found WITHOUT this one (drift; see docs "known gaps")
#   VM.PowerMgmt / VM.Console                   power + VNC console
#   VM.Backup                                   vzdump 403s without it => customer backups dead
#   VM.Snapshot / VM.Snapshot.Rollback          snapshots + restore
#   VM.Audit                                    read status/config/RRD
#   VM.GuestAgent.Audit                         in-guest disk sampling (get-fsinfo)
#   VM.GuestAgent.FileRead                      in-guest MEMORY sampling (reads /proc/meminfo via the agent's
#                                               file-read). Missing => ServerMemSample silently empty and the
#                                               admin/customer RAM graphs fall back to the balloon number.
#   SDN.Use                                     PVE 9: attaching a NIC to vmbr1 is permission-checked under
#                                               /sdn/zones/localnetwork/vmbr1
#   Datastore.* / Pool.Allocate                 allocate disks/cloud-init drives, list storage
#   Sys.Audit / Sys.Console / Sys.Modify        node status, shell-ish operations, storage/snippet content
# DO NOT add VM.Monitor: removed in PVE 9, `pveum role modify` rejects the whole call.
NXEON_CANON_ROLE_PRIVS=(
  Datastore.Allocate Datastore.AllocateSpace Datastore.AllocateTemplate Datastore.Audit
  Pool.Allocate SDN.Use
  Sys.Audit Sys.Console Sys.Modify
  VM.Allocate VM.Audit VM.Backup VM.Clone
  VM.Config.CDROM VM.Config.CPU VM.Config.Cloudinit VM.Config.Disk VM.Config.HWType
  VM.Config.Memory VM.Config.Network VM.Config.Options
  VM.Console VM.GuestAgent.Audit VM.GuestAgent.FileRead
  VM.PowerMgmt VM.Snapshot VM.Snapshot.Rollback
)

nxeon_role_privs_csv() { local IFS=,; echo "${NXEON_CANON_ROLE_PRIVS[*]}"; }

# ---------- OS templates every node must carry --------------------------------
# vmid|proxmox-name|OsTemplate.slug(s) it backs (informational)
# Every active OsTemplate row in the DB points at one of these vmids; the
# scheduler does NOT check template availability per node, so a node missing
# one will receive an order for that OS and fail the clone.
NXEON_CANON_TEMPLATES=(
  "9000|tpl-ubuntu-2404|ubuntu-24-04"
  "9001|tpl-debian-13|debian-13"
  "9002|tpl-almalinux-9|almalinux-9"
  "9003|tpl-rocky-9|rocky-9"
  "9004|tpl-ubuntu-22-04|ubuntu-22-04"
  "9005|tpl-debian-12|debian-12"
  "9006|tpl-ubuntu-20-04|ubuntu-20-04"
  "9007|tpl-almalinux-8|almalinux-8"
  "9008|tpl-rocky-8|rocky-8"
  "9009|tpl-debian-11|debian-11"
)
nxeon_canon_template_ids() { local t; for t in "${NXEON_CANON_TEMPLATES[@]}"; do echo "${t%%|*}"; done; }

# ---------- Cloud-init vendor snippet (byte-identical on every node) ----------
# sha256 of this exact text is what every live node has at
# <snippets-storage>/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml (verified 2026-10-01).
nxeon_vendor_snippet() {
  cat <<'EOF'
#cloud-config
package_update: true
packages:
  - qemu-guest-agent
ssh_pwauth: true
disable_root: false
write_files:
  - path: /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/60-nxeon.conf
    permissions: "0644"
    content: |
      PermitRootLogin yes
      PasswordAuthentication yes
runcmd:
  - systemctl enable --now qemu-guest-agent
  - systemctl restart ssh || systemctl restart sshd
EOF
}

# ---------- Per-node network derivation --------------------------------------
# nxeon_derive_net NODE_NUM [SUBNET_OCTET]
# Sets (globals): D_OCTET D_SUBNET_PREFIX D_SUBNET_CIDR D_GATEWAY D_NAT_CHAIN
# Convention (matches every existing node): node N -> 10.20.(N-1).0/24, chain
# NXEON_FWD for N<=1 else NXEON_FWD_N<N>.
nxeon_derive_net() {
  local n="$1" oct="${2:-}"
  [[ "$n" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && (( n >= 1 && n <= 250 )) || { echo "invalid node number: $n" >&2; return 1; }
  [[ -z "$oct" ]] && oct=$((n - 1))
  [[ "$oct" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && (( oct >= 0 && oct <= 254 )) || { echo "invalid subnet octet: $oct" >&2; return 1; }
  D_OCTET="$oct"
  D_SUBNET_PREFIX="10.20.${oct}."
  D_SUBNET_CIDR="10.20.${oct}.0/24"
  D_GATEWAY="10.20.${oct}.1"
  if (( n <= 1 )); then D_NAT_CHAIN="NXEON_FWD"; else D_NAT_CHAIN="NXEON_FWD_N${n}"; fi
}

# Capacity RAM (MB) the Add-node form should carry: physical RAM minus an 8 GB
# host reserve. Matches every live row (56000/56171/23862/56070 for 64/64/32/64 GB).
nxeon_capacity_ram_mb() { local total_mb="$1"; echo $(( total_mb - 8000 )); }

# ---------- Host tuning constants --------------------------------------------
NXEON_CANON_ARC_GB_DEFAULT=8        # ZFS ARC cap; primary/node-3/4/5 precedent
NXEON_CANON_ARC_MIN_GB=2            # below this is almost certainly a mistake (node-2 sat at 0.4 GB)
NXEON_CANON_ARC_MAX_GB=16
NXEON_CANON_JOURNAL_MAX="500M"      # primary precedent; nodes 2-5 had NO cap
NXEON_CANON_CONNTRACK_MIN=262144
NXEON_CANON_BACKUP_MAX_ROOT_PCT=85  # root fs fill level that is a FAIL
NXEON_CANON_BACKUP_STALE_HOURS=36   # newest platform archive older than this => FAIL

# /etc/sysctl.d/99-nxeon.conf content (ip_forward is the only hard requirement;
# the NAT bridge's post-up also sets it, but that does not survive an `ifreload`).
nxeon_sysctl_conf() {
  cat <<'EOF'
# Nxeon compute node — written by scripts/onboard-node.sh
net.ipv4.ip_forward = 1
EOF
}

# ---------- Provider/region validation (mirror of lib/node-regions.ts) --------
# Only used for an early warning in onboard-node.sh; the app's own validation is
# authoritative.
nxeon_region_valid() {
  local provider="$1" region="$2" r
  local -a list
  case "$provider" in
    OVH)     list=(sgp1 bhs1 gra1 rbx1 waw1) ;;
    HETZNER) list=(fsn1 nbg1 hel1 ash1 hil1) ;;
    *) return 1 ;;
  esac
  for r in "${list[@]}"; do [[ "$r" == "$region" ]] && return 0; done
  return 1
}

# ---------- Template config normalisation ------------------------------------
# Reads `qm config <id>` on stdin, drops the per-clone/per-host noise (MAC,
# vmgenid, smbios uuid, meta, creds), and folds the cicustom storage name to
# "<S>" because the primary calls it `backup` while nodes call it `vmdata-hdd`
# (both resolve to the same snippets dir; the `backup` alias exists for exactly
# that). Two templates are "identical" iff their normalised text is equal.
nxeon_normalize_template_config() {
  grep -v -E '^(net0|ide2|vmgenid|smbios1|meta|ciuser|sshkeys|cipassword|digest|parent|lock):' \
    | sed -E 's#^(cicustom: vendor=)[^:]+:#\1<S>:#' \
    | LC_ALL=C sort
}

# Human-readable PVE storage.cfg parsing helpers ------------------------------
# nxeon_storage_attr <storage.cfg path> <storage-id> <key>   -> value or empty
nxeon_storage_attr() {
  awk -v sid="$2" -v key="$3" '
    /^[a-z]+:[ \t]/ { cur=$2; next }
    cur==sid && $1==key { $1=""; sub(/^[ \t]+/,""); print; exit }
  ' "$1"
}

#   VM.GuestAgent.FileRead                      in-guest MEMORY sampling (reads /proc/meminfo via the agent's
#                                               file-read). Missing => ServerMemSample silently empty and the
#                                               admin/customer RAM graphs fall back to the balloon number.
#   SDN.Use                                     PVE 9: attaching a NIC to vmbr1 is permission-checked under
#                                               /sdn/zones/localnetwork/vmbr1
#   Datastore.* / Pool.Allocate                 allocate disks/cloud-init drives, list storage
#   Sys.Audit / Sys.Console / Sys.Modify        node status, shell-ish operations, storage/snippet content
# DO NOT add VM.Monitor: removed in PVE 9, `pveum role modify` rejects the whole call.
NXEON_CANON_ROLE_PRIVS=(
  Datastore.Allocate Datastore.AllocateSpace Datastore.AllocateTemplate Datastore.Audit
  Pool.Allocate SDN.Use
  Sys.Audit Sys.Console Sys.Modify
  VM.Allocate VM.Audit VM.Backup VM.Clone
  VM.Config.CDROM VM.Config.CPU VM.Config.Cloudinit VM.Config.Disk VM.Config.HWType
  VM.Config.Memory VM.Config.Network VM.Config.Options
  VM.Console VM.GuestAgent.Audit VM.GuestAgent.FileRead
  VM.PowerMgmt VM.Snapshot VM.Snapshot.Rollback
)

nxeon_role_privs_csv() { local IFS=,; echo "${NXEON_CANON_ROLE_PRIVS[*]}"; }

# ---------- OS templates every node must carry --------------------------------
# vmid|proxmox-name|OsTemplate.slug(s) it backs (informational)
# Every active OsTemplate row in the DB points at one of these vmids; the
# scheduler does NOT check template availability per node, so a node missing
# one will receive an order for that OS and fail the clone.
NXEON_CANON_TEMPLATES=(
  "9000|tpl-ubuntu-2404|ubuntu-24-04"
  "9001|tpl-debian-13|debian-13"
  "9002|tpl-almalinux-9|almalinux-9"
  "9003|tpl-rocky-9|rocky-9"
  "9004|tpl-ubuntu-22-04|ubuntu-22-04"
  "9005|tpl-debian-12|debian-12"
  "9006|tpl-ubuntu-20-04|ubuntu-20-04"
  "9007|tpl-almalinux-8|almalinux-8"
  "9008|tpl-rocky-8|rocky-8"
  "9009|tpl-debian-11|debian-11"
)
nxeon_canon_template_ids() { local t; for t in "${NXEON_CANON_TEMPLATES[@]}"; do echo "${t%%|*}"; done; }

# ---------- Cloud-init vendor snippet (byte-identical on every node) ----------
# sha256 of this exact text is what every live node has at
# <snippets-storage>/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml (verified 2026-10-01).
nxeon_vendor_snippet() {
  cat <<'EOF'
#cloud-config
package_update: true
packages:
  - qemu-guest-agent
ssh_pwauth: true
disable_root: false
write_files:
  - path: /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/60-nxeon.conf
    permissions: "0644"
    content: |
      PermitRootLogin yes
      PasswordAuthentication yes
runcmd:
  - systemctl enable --now qemu-guest-agent
  - systemctl restart ssh || systemctl restart sshd
EOF
}

# ---------- Per-node network derivation --------------------------------------
# nxeon_derive_net NODE_NUM [SUBNET_OCTET]
# Sets (globals): D_OCTET D_SUBNET_PREFIX D_SUBNET_CIDR D_GATEWAY D_NAT_CHAIN
# Convention (matches every existing node): node N -> 10.20.(N-1).0/24, chain
# NXEON_FWD for N<=1 else NXEON_FWD_N<N>.
nxeon_derive_net() {
  local n="$1" oct="${2:-}"
  [[ "$n" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && (( n >= 1 && n <= 250 )) || { echo "invalid node number: $n" >&2; return 1; }
  [[ -z "$oct" ]] && oct=$((n - 1))
  [[ "$oct" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && (( oct >= 0 && oct <= 254 )) || { echo "invalid subnet octet: $oct" >&2; return 1; }
  D_OCTET="$oct"
  D_SUBNET_PREFIX="10.20.${oct}."
  D_SUBNET_CIDR="10.20.${oct}.0/24"
  D_GATEWAY="10.20.${oct}.1"
  if (( n <= 1 )); then D_NAT_CHAIN="NXEON_FWD"; else D_NAT_CHAIN="NXEON_FWD_N${n}"; fi
}

# Capacity RAM (MB) the Add-node form should carry: physical RAM minus an 8 GB
# host reserve. Matches every live row (56000/56171/23862/56070 for 64/64/32/64 GB).
nxeon_capacity_ram_mb() { local total_mb="$1"; echo $(( total_mb - 8000 )); }

# ---------- Host tuning constants --------------------------------------------
NXEON_CANON_ARC_GB_DEFAULT=8        # ZFS ARC cap; primary/node-3/4/5 precedent
NXEON_CANON_ARC_MIN_GB=2            # below this is almost certainly a mistake (node-2 sat at 0.4 GB)
NXEON_CANON_ARC_MAX_GB=16
NXEON_CANON_JOURNAL_MAX="500M"      # primary precedent; nodes 2-5 had NO cap
NXEON_CANON_CONNTRACK_MIN=262144
NXEON_CANON_BACKUP_MAX_ROOT_PCT=85  # root fs fill level that is a FAIL
NXEON_CANON_BACKUP_STALE_HOURS=36   # newest platform archive older than this => FAIL

# /etc/sysctl.d/99-nxeon.conf content (ip_forward is the only hard requirement;
# the NAT bridge's post-up also sets it, but that does not survive an `ifreload`).
nxeon_sysctl_conf() {
  cat <<'EOF'
# Nxeon compute node — written by scripts/onboard-node.sh
net.ipv4.ip_forward = 1
EOF
}

# ---------- Provider/region validation (mirror of lib/node-regions.ts) --------
# Only used for an early warning in onboard-node.sh; the app's own validation is
# authoritative.
nxeon_region_valid() {
  local provider="$1" region="$2" r
  local -a list
  case "$provider" in
    OVH)     list=(sgp1 bhs1 gra1 rbx1 waw1) ;;
    HETZNER) list=(fsn1 nbg1 hel1 ash1 hil1) ;;
    *) return 1 ;;
  esac
  for r in "${list[@]}"; do [[ "$r" == "$region" ]] && return 0; done
  return 1
}

# ---------- Template config normalisation ------------------------------------
# Reads `qm config <id>` on stdin, drops the per-clone/per-host noise (MAC,
# vmgenid, smbios uuid, meta, creds), and folds the cicustom storage name to
# "<S>" because the primary calls it `backup` while nodes call it `vmdata-hdd`
# (both resolve to the same snippets dir; the `backup` alias exists for exactly
# that). Two templates are "identical" iff their normalised text is equal.
nxeon_normalize_template_config() {
  grep -v -E '^(net0|ide2|vmgenid|smbios1|meta|ciuser|sshkeys|cipassword|digest|parent|lock):' \
    | sed -E 's#^(cicustom: vendor=)[^:]+:#\1<S>:#' \
    | LC_ALL=C sort
}

# Human-readable PVE storage.cfg parsing helpers ------------------------------
# nxeon_storage_attr <storage.cfg path> <storage-id> <key>   -> value or empty
nxeon_storage_attr() {
  awk -v sid="$2" -v key="$3" '
    /^[a-z]+:[ \t]/ { cur=$2; next }
    cur==sid && $1==key { $1=""; sub(/^[ \t]+/,""); print; exit }
  ' "$1"
}
