Paste the printed values. Fields and gotchas:
`Provider server ID` and `Monthly cost` are not discoverable from the box (see pre-flight 4; leave blank
rather than guess — a wrong id only fails when the first dedicated-IP is allocated); `Region` must be the
code you validated; `Capacity RAM MB` = physical − 8000 (printed); Agent port/token from the script.
**Leave `enabled` OFF** (and optionally `acceptsProvisions` off) → run **Test node** (Proxmox API + node-agent
health) → then from the primary: `scripts/verify-node.sh node-N` (adds the DB, reachability, template-coverage
and memory-sampling checks the node cannot see itself).

#### 5. DNS

No per-node DNS record is required: customer-facing names resolve to *server* addresses (game subdomain
A/SRV records are built from each server's node `publicIp` by `worker/game-subdomain-sync.ts`, no region
logic). Optional: a `nxeon-<region><n>.nxeon.cloud` A record for the hostname (node-2 has one) — purely
cosmetic. `host.hostname` only needs `/etc/hosts` to resolve the hostname.

#### 6. Mail / blocklist / provider-side

Outbound port 25 policy, reverse DNS of the node IP and any provider-side firewall are provider settings —
check them in the provider console now; none are scriptable from the box.

#### 7. Region + marketing wiring (ONLY when the datacenter is new to Nxeon)

An existing region (a 2nd Singapore node) needs nothing here. A new datacenter needs, in one commit
(`verify: db.region_code` WARNs until done; `tsc` enforces the first):
1. `lib/node-regions.ts` — add to `NODE_REGIONS` and **every** strict table (`REGION_LABELS`,
   `CUSTOMER_REGION_LABELS`, `REGION_COUNTRY`, `REGION_COORDS`).
2. `lib/nx/catalog.ts` `COORDS` (area + latency hint for the deploy wizard; the wizard groups the region
   picker by `area`).
3. `components/nx/Bits.tsx` — country flag entry (a missing one once shipped a US flag on the Canada server).
4. `lib/marketing/locationLandings.ts` — a `datacenter` landing (`slug` = lower-cased customer label,
   e.g. `canada`), then regenerate the per-game location pages with `tools/nxm` (never hand-edit
   `app/nxm/<game>-server-hosting/<slug>/page.tsx` or `app/nxm/_data/live-routes.json` — Canada shipped 404s
   for every game until these were generated).
5. Honest copy only: Nxeon speaks as the owner; never name the infrastructure provider to customers.

#### 8. Smoke test with a throwaway server, then enable

With the node still `enabled=false`/`acceptsProvisions=false`, create a throwaway **VPS** and a **game
server** pinned to it (admin test account, brand-new VMIDs only — never reuse an id):
- guest agent up; web terminal; file manager; console/RCON (game); backup create + restore;
- a **real external SSH connection** to the node's NAT-forwarded port from a *separate host on another
  provider* (a guest-agent ping proves cloud-init ran, **not** that the NAT hop works);
- `iptables -t nat -S NXEON_FWD_N<N>` on the node shows the DNAT rule (chain created by the agent);
- memory sampling: a fresh `ServerMemSample` row appears for the server within ~5 min (`db.mem_samples`) — this is
  the `VM.GuestAgent.FileRead` path;

```bash
scripts/verify-node.sh node-N          # one node, full report + exact fix per finding
scripts/verify-node.sh --all           # whole fleet + matrix; run weekly / after any node change
scripts/verify-node.sh --all --quiet   # only WARN/FAIL
```
Exit 0 = no FAIL. `--strict` makes WARN fail too. Optional `--api-token 'nxeon@pve!platform=SECRET'` adds an
authenticated Proxmox API probe. The verifier never writes to the node (the remote probe is shipped as one
`bash -c` argument and leaves no file behind).

#### 10. Rollback

- **Firewall**: auto-reverts unless `--confirm`ed; manual: `nft delete table inet nxeon_fw` (or the provider KVM).
- **Not yet enabled in the DB**: nothing to roll back platform-side — delete the `Node` row.
- **Host**: the script never destroys storage or VMs. Reverse a step by hand: `ifdown vmbrN` + remove the

  asking the owner**); `systemctl disable --now nxeon-node-agent nxeon-backup-vms.timer`.
- A node with live customers is never "rolled back": migrate them off (see "Migrating a customer…") first.

#### What `verify-node.sh` checks (ids are stable)

`host.*` PVE services, hostname, repos, time sync, unattended-upgrades, SMART, journald cap, root-disk headroom,
ZFS health, **ARC cap persisted + live + sane (2-16 GB)**, ip_forward, conntrack, SSH hardening/primary key, kernel ·

`db.*` row fields, uniqueness, capacity, cost, provider id format, region validity + repo wiring, agent token/port,
OsTemplate coverage, memory samples flowing.

nodes (results above). No live node was modified.

input.message:
Branch `docs/node-onboarding-vetting`, worktree `/opt/nxeon-wt-nodedocs`, one commit `65f1de847c`. No live node was modified. I did not run onboard-node.sh end to end on a host (nothing safe to run it on); everything else was run for real.

**Shipped (all in `scripts/` plus the docs):**
- `node-canon.sh` (new, sourced by the other scripts). It holds the canonical 27-privilege role, templates 9000-9009, the byte-exact vendor snippet, network derivation and testable helpers.
- `verify-node.sh` (new). Read-only, about 75 stable-id checks, prints the exact fix command for every FAIL/WARN, exits 1 on any FAIL, and `--all` prints a fleet matrix.
- `export-templates.sh` (new). Runs on the primary and dumps templates 9000-9009 plus `SHA256SUMS`, so a new node gets identical images.
- `onboard-node.sh` (rewritten). The `--skip-*` flags are kept and `--plan` is new. It now covers:
  - `--node-num` is required; the old default of 2 is gone.
  - The canonical role is re-applied on every run.
  - Templates are restored with `--templates-dir`.
  - The backup volume is never left on `/`; a same-pool ZFS dataset is carved.
  - Tuning baseline: ARC cap, journald cap, chrony, unattended-upgrades, SMART, repos.
  - The firewall allowlist is seeded with the primary and your SSH IP, and `--apply-firewall` applies it through safe-apply.
  - fail2ban `ignoreip` includes the primary.
  - The backup timer is enabled and started.
  - It self-verifies at the end and saves the Add-node values to a 0600 file.
- `test-node-scripts.sh` (new): 63 unit checks of the pure parts, all pass.
- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md`: the "Adding node N" section is now the single runbook (provider-console region/zone check through rollback). I added a "Known gaps found on existing nodes" section with exact owner fix commands, plus a change-history entry.

**Verification:** I ran `verify-node.sh --all` against all five nodes over real SSH. shellcheck at warning level is clean apart from two harmless unused-variable notes. Not covered: the first real onboarding (node-6) should be run with `--plan` first and watched.

**Matrix (FAIL unless marked warn):**
| finding | primary | node-2 | node-3 | node-4 | node-5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| templates missing | ok | 9005-9009 | ok | 9005-9009 | 9001, 9005-9009 |
| backup volume on the root fs | ok | ok | ok | ok | yes |
| root disk 95-96% full | yes | ok | ok | ok | yes |
| backup timer dead, archives 19 days old | ok | yes | ok | ok | ok |
| role missing `Sys.Modify` and `VM.Config.Options` | yes | ok | ok | ok | ok |
| firewall file older than repo (warn) | n/a | warn | warn | warn | warn |
| primary not in fail2ban `ignoreip` (warn) | n/a | warn | warn | warn | warn |
| journald uncapped (warn) | ok | warn | warn | warn | warn |
| SSH password login on (warn) | warn | ok | warn | warn | warn |
| ARC cap 0.4 GB (warn) | ok | warn | ok | ok | ok |
| no unattended-upgrades (warn) | ok | warn | ok | ok | ok |

node-3 has no FAILs. The agent code, systemd units, vendor snippet and sysctls are identical across nodes, and memory samples are flowing everywhere.

**Owner actions, most urgent first (exact commands are in the docs "known gaps" section):**
1. **Missing templates** on node-2, node-4 and node-5. All three have `acceptsProvisions=true` and `scheduleNode()` doesn't check templates, so a Debian 12, Ubuntu 20.04, Alma 8 or Rocky 8 order placed there fails at clone. Turn off "accepts new servers" on those nodes until the templates are restored.
2. **node-5 backups on the 20 GB root fs** (96% full). Carve `data/backup` the way node-3 did, before copying templates there.
3. **node-2 backup timer**: `systemctl enable --now nxeon-backup-vms.timer`. Also raise its ARC cap and install unattended-upgrades.
4. **Primary role**: add the two missing privileges. The primary also has a leftover test role/user/token (`NxeonProvisionerScoped`, `nxeon-scoped-test@pve`, `validation`) to clean up if unneeded.
5. Firewall rollout on nodes 2-5, fail2ban `ignoreip`, journald cap, SSH password auth.
6. The primary's root disk is 95% full and its swap is exhausted. That is not an onboarding gap, but the verifier correctly flags the disk.

**Outside my area, not done:** `scheduleNode()` in `lib/node-capacity.ts` should skip nodes lacking the order's template. I did not spawn a task for it.

**Needs owner approval/run:** the first attempt to `source .env` and `select *` from the Node table was denied by the auto-mode classifier, so I did not retry it. I used non-secret columns only via `sudo -u postgres psql`.

No schema changes. No files edited outside my area.

content.text:
I've committed the node-onboarding work to `docs/node-onboarding-vetting` (worktree `/opt/nxeon-wt-nodedocs`, commit `65f1de847c`) and delivered the report to the caller. No live node was changed.

The audit found real problems on the existing nodes:

- **Missing templates on nodes 2, 4 and 5:** node-2 and node-4 lack 9005-9009; node-5 also lacks 9001. They accept orders and the scheduler doesn't check templates, so some OS orders will fail at clone. Turn off "accepts new servers" on those three until the templates are restored.
- **node-5 backups on the 20 GB root disk:** the backup volume is a directory on a 20 GB root partition that is 96% full.
- **node-2 backups:** the backup timer is enabled but dead, so its last archive is 19 days old. Its ZFS cache cap is also only 0.4 GB.
- **Primary role:** it lacks `Sys.Modify` and `VM.Config.Options`.
- **Smaller drift on nodes 2-5:** firewall rules older than the repo copy, and journald uncapped. The primary isn't exempt from fail2ban bans, and password SSH login is still on for the primary, node-3, node-4 and node-5 (node-2 already has it off).
- **Primary root disk (not an onboarding gap):** it is 95% full and its swap is exhausted.

What changed in the repo:

- **`node-canon.sh`:** one shared definition of a correct node, including the full 27-privilege role.
- **`verify-node.sh`:** a read-only checker that prints the exact fix command for each finding and has a `--all` fleet matrix.
- **`export-templates.sh`:** a primary-side template export.
- **`onboard-node.sh`:** rewritten to build everything the verifier checks, then self-verify.
- **Tests and docs:** 63 unit checks in `test-node-scripts.sh`, and the Adding-node-N runbook in `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` replaced with a rewritten one plus the known-gaps list and exact owner fix commands.

I ran `verify-node.sh` for real against all five nodes. I did not run `onboard-node.sh` end to end on a fresh host. The first real onboarding (node-6) should start with `--plan` and be watched. The full matrix and the owner action list are in the report.

One follow-up is not done: `scheduleNode()` in `lib/node-capacity.ts` should skip nodes that lack the order's template. It is outside this task's area and I did not spawn a task for it.
